skill.name: polars
skill.description: Provides practical Polars guidance for expression-based DataFrame analysis, lazy pipelines, transformations, pandas migration, and file, database, and cloud I/O.
skill.summary: Build efficient Polars transformations and data pipelines with focused examples and performance guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 95 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, ordinary Polars terminology, placeholder cloud configuration, and the Polars list.eval API. The reviewed files contain documentation and fixed examples, with no prompt injection, credential harvesting, shell substitution, dynamic code execution, or system reconnaissance.

static_findings.snippet: For additional best practices and patterns, load `references/best_practices.md`.
- `core_concepts.md` - Detailed explanations of expressions, lazy evaluation, and type system
- `operations.md` - Comprehensive guide to all common operations with examples
- `pandas_migration.md` - Complete migration guide from pandas to Polars
- `io_guide.md` - Data I/O operations for all supported formats
- `transformations.md` - Joins, concatenation, pivots, and reshaping operations

content.user_title: Build Faster Data Pipelines with Polars
content.value_statement: Large DataFrame workflows can become slow and memory intensive. This skill provides Polars patterns for efficient transformations, lazy execution, I/O, and pandas migration.
actual_capabilities: Guides DataFrame creation, selection, filtering, calculated columns, grouping, aggregation, sorting, and window operations.
Explains lazy execution, streaming, query optimization, schema handling, and memory-conscious processing.
Covers CSV, Parquet, JSON, Excel, database, cloud storage, Arrow, NumPy, and pandas I/O patterns.
Provides patterns for joins, concatenation, pivoting, unpivoting, exploding, and nested data transformations.
Maps common pandas workflows to Polars expressions and identifies migration pitfalls.
limitations: The skill does not execute pipelines or inspect datasets unless the active environment provides those capabilities.
Examples target Python Polars and may require changes for different package versions.
Cloud and database examples require user-configured dependencies, connectivity, permissions, and credentials.
Performance guidance does not replace benchmarking with representative data and production hardware.

use_cases.title: Migrate pandas Analysis
use_cases.description: Translate indexed, grouped, and column-oriented pandas workflows into strict, expression-based Polars operations.

use_cases.title: Design Large File Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan lazy CSV or Parquet processing with early filters, selected columns, streaming, and efficient output formats.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Data
use_cases.description: Build reproducible cleaning, reshaping, aggregation, and feature preparation workflows for structured datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Polars DataFrame
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to create a Polars DataFrame from [sample data], select columns, filter rows, and add one calculated column.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Lazy File Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a lazy Polars workflow for [file format] that filters [condition], selects [columns], aggregates [metric], and writes [output format].

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a Pandas Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this pandas workflow to idiomatic Polars: [workflow]. Explain index differences, expression contexts, type behavior, and any semantic changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Replacing pandas in an existing analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Polars pipeline: [pipeline]. Identify blocked optimizations, memory risks, schema issues, and expensive joins, then propose a validated improvement plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Tuning a complex production data pipeline.

output_examples.input: Summarize monthly sales by region from a large CSV file.
output: Start with a lazy CSV scan and select only the required date, region, and sales columns.
Filter invalid rows before grouping by month and region.
Aggregate sales, sort the result, then collect or write the final table.

output_examples.input: Convert a pandas group transform workflow to Polars.
output_examples.output: Use native Polars expressions inside a grouped window operation, preserving row count without a pandas index.

output_examples.input: Reduce memory use in a multi-file Parquet pipeline.
output: Scan files lazily, declare stable types, and project required columns before joins.
Apply selective filters early and use streaming output when the operation supports it.
Benchmark the revised plan with representative files before deployment.

best_practices: Provide sample schemas, expected output, and representative row values when requesting a transformation.
Prefer lazy scans, early filtering, and early column selection for large file workflows.
Confirm the installed Polars version and benchmark performance changes with representative data.
anti_patterns: Do not request row-by-row Python loops when native Polars expressions can perform the operation.
Avoid placing production credentials directly in prompts, examples, or generated source files.
Do not assume pandas index behavior or silent type conversion applies to Polars.

faq.question: What Polars topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers expressions, lazy execution, transformations, aggregations, I/O, optimization, and pandas migration.

faq.question: Can it migrate pandas code?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps common pandas operations to Polars and explains index, typing, parallelism, and expression differences.

faq.question: Does the skill execute data pipelines?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples; execution depends on the active agent tools and environment.

faq.question: Which data formats are included?
faq.answer: The references cover CSV, Parquet, JSON, Excel, databases, cloud storage, Arrow, NumPy, and pandas.

faq.question: Can it improve pipeline performance?
faq.answer: It can suggest lazy evaluation, streaming, pushdown, efficient types, and join improvements that users should benchmark.

faq.question: Does cloud I/O require credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Users must configure provider credentials and permissions securely outside shared prompts and committed source files.
